reviewed_high_risk.rationale: RA2: /stackvox-install and /stackvox-upgrade start the local stackvox text-to-speech daemon with nohup, which is the documented purpose of those commands. TM1: /stackvox-uninstall deletes only the stackvox model cache (after asking the user) and the plugin's own check stamp.

RA2: the SessionStart hook boots the local stackvox daemon, and the Codex hook scripts re-run themselves in the background because Codex does not support async hooks. SC2: check-install.sh reads the stackvox version from the PyPI JSON API at most once a week to suggest /stackvox-upgrade; nothing it fetches is executed.
Generated Codex adapter for the stackvox-install command: starting the local stackvox text-to-speech daemon with nohup is the documented purpose, reviewed with the command itself.
Generated Codex adapter for the stackvox-upgrade command: restarting the local stackvox daemon after the upgrade is the documented purpose, reviewed with the command itself.
Generated Codex adapter for the stackvox-uninstall command: it deletes only the stackvox model cache, after asking the user, and the plugin's own check stamp, as reviewed for the command itself.

SC6 misidentifies the optional-dependency group key test as a package resembling pytest, and the established scientific dependencies scipy and six as resembling scrapy and pip. The group installs pytest, not a package named test. SciPy provides image processing and six is required by python-dateutil; their exact distributions are pinned with hashes in requirements.lock. This exception covers package-name similarity only; vulnerability findings remain blocking. AST4 and OH1: test_pr_review.py starts the current Python interpreter with a fixed import/assertion program and no shell to verify cache isolation in a fresh process; capture_output is a subprocess option, not executable external output. The child uses test-owned config/cache paths and no input from charts, users or network sources.

AST4: ocr.py and benchmark_support.py call the user-installed Tesseract with argument lists and no shell, for local OCR and version metadata. OH1 matches the capture_output keyword on the constant tesseract --version command; neither OCR nor model output becomes a command. LP3: local image/file processing, output folders, the runtime X_BEARER_TOKEN and opt-in public network retrieval are documented in SKILL.md and README; no hooks or automatic installs run. E1: collect.py sends that token only as authorization to the fixed https://api.x.com/2/ endpoint for the requested public lookup/search. EA2: external_evidence.py records a selection_uses label describing numerical fitting dates; it does not grant autonomous actions or change permissions.
